vectors.name: truthy-function-is-truthy
vectors.note: A function is neither false nor null, so it is truthy. §5.4's restrictions are about values, not truthiness.

vectors.name: truthy-filter-uses-the-same-rule
vectors.note: filter reads truthiness identically to if: 0 and "" survive, false and null do not.

vectors.name: equal-exact-above-2-53
vectors.note: The spec's own case. Converting the int to a float makes these indistinguishable, so an implementation that compares by conversion agrees below 2^53 and then diverges silently -- exactly what §11 exists to catch.

vectors.name: equal-deep-maps-regardless-of-construction-order
vectors.note: Maps are ordered by key, so construction order cannot make two equal maps unequal.

vectors.name: equal-across-types-is-false-not-an-error
vectors.note: Different types are unequal; only a function operand is an error.

vectors.name: equal-function-left-is-type-error
vectors.note: A function has no identity to compare. Answering false would let a mistyped comparison evaluate quietly forever.

vectors.name: equal-negative-zero-equals-zero
vectors.note: IEEE 754 numeric equality: -0.0 = 0.0, even though §7.6 renders them differently and ABI §6.3.1 preserves the sign.
